transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I can't sleep properly.
Can you tell me when your sleep problem started, how it came on, whether anything seemed to set it off, and if you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
Started about three months ago, when I retired.
Could you tell me how your sleep problem affects your daily life, and what medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently—and how much you take, if you know?
Too tired to work on my allotment.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines—yes, no, or you're not sure?
No, none that I know of.
Have you ever had any operations or been in hospital for anything?
No, never been in hospital for anything.
How much of a problem is your sleep at the moment — a small problem, a medium problem, or a big problem, or you’re not sure?
Big problem. About seven out of ten.
Have you noticed any other symptoms that seem to go together with your sleep problem?
My mood's been low since I retired.
Are you taking any medicines at the moment — ones you take every day, ones you only take now and then, or none at all — or are you not sure?
Losartan once a day, for my blood pressure.
Where, if anywhere, do you notice this problem in your body?
My daughter keeps saying I should get out more.
What makes your sleep better or worse?
Worse after late nights watching TV.
When it comes to your sleep, does it bother you most nights, or does it tend to come and go?
Most nights.
When sleep is not going well, where do you notice it most — in one place, in a few places, or all over — or are you not sure?
I just feel shattered all over.
What worries you most about your sleep right now, and what are you hoping to get from this visit?
Hoping you can give me proper sleeping tablets.
Is there anything else about your past health you think would be helpful to mention?
I've got an enlarged prostate.
When you can't sleep, what is that like for you?
I wake at three or four and can't get back.
You've mentioned feeling low since retiring and feeling shattered all over — is there anything else you've noticed about how you're feeling that you'd like to add?
Since the divorce, I don't really see many people.
When you wake at three or four and can't get back to sleep, is that more a physical feeling for you, more an emotional feeling, or you're not sure?
Not sure. Just lying there awake.
Is there anything else about your past health that you'd like to add?
I take tamsulosin at night too.
Are there any other medicines you take that we haven't talked about yet?
I've been taking sleeping tablets from the pharmacy.
Anything else you've noticed since your sleep changed?
I doze off in the chair in the afternoon.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
